title: Recheck cancellation after installing a listener across user callbacks
applies_when: An API checks an AbortSignal, calls a user callback or converts a thenable, and only afterward installs its rejection listener; or listener registration itself calls user code before storing the listener. Cancellation can occur synchronously without any await or another thread.
lesson: Separate observing current cancellation state from subscribing to future events. AbortSignal does not replay an earlier abort to a newly added listener. In p-queue 9.3.4, a callback can abort before returning a pending operation; the add promise then stays pending, retains its concurrency slot and blocks the next task. Register the running listener and check signal.aborted so a past event follows the same rejection path. Keep cleanup and promise-race handling intact rather than throwing early and abandoning a returned rejected promise. Use a controlled operation gate: inspect settlement and follower progress before release, then always release it for cleanup. Test async-function synchronous prefixes and thenable conversion as well as plain callbacks; retain normal completion, pre-abort, microtask-abort and task-error precedence controls. Also inspect registration itself: Node EventEmitter emits newListener before inserting the listener. In p-event 8.0.0, an abort there correctly rejects but cleanup runs too early to remove that pending insertion. Recheck termination after addListener returns and remove the exact listener if needed. Pair native newListener controls with existing post-registration replay tests; preserve caller-owned listeners and the original abort reason.
avoid_when: Follow the actual cancellation contract: rejecting a queue wait does not stop the underlying operation, and the caller still owns its cleanup. This single-event-loop pattern is not an atomic cross-thread subscription protocol. Already returned values can still win the existing Promise.race; the queue repair deliberately preserves that behavior and original callback-error precedence. Queue evidence is 208 Windows runtime tests plus tsc/tsd and eight public-API cases per arm on Windows and Linux, not full Linux/Node20 CI. Queue lint has nine project-service errors on both unchanged and patched source. The p-event repair passes 158 runtime tests plus XO/tsd on native Windows/Linux Node24; six native newListener regressions fail before it. This is not the Node22/26 CI matrix or proof against every custom emitter exception/reentrancy pattern. A correctly rejected promise alone does not prove listener cleanup; mocks which store first or never store can hide this defect. Both patches are published on forks with issues because upstream PR creation is collaborators-only; no acceptance, measured Scout conversion or prospective selector advantage is claimed.

evidence.note: The task callback runs before the running abort listener is installed. Promise conversion for task timeouts can also invoke a then getter in this interval. This source identifies the handoff; the public-package probe establishes its behavior.

Standalone npm9.3.4 reproduction and bounded native result: three affected callback/conversion cases retain pending=1 before the operation gate is released; the repair rejects with the abort reason, releases capacity and starts the follower. Five controls and cleanup remain unchanged on both native platforms. Owner-led manual discovery, not a prospective experiment or paid Scout result.

Four-line production addition and a real-queue regression test. The regression fails on unchanged source and passes after the state recheck; the existing finally block removes the listener. Fork commit only, not an upstream PR or merge.
The native newListener event runs before the new listener is added to the internal listener array. This documents the ordering, not p-event correctness or a measured memory footprint.

Public native EventEmitter reproduction on main421ea1a/8.0.0: aborting during data/error registration leaves that listener attached in all three exports. Six regressions fail before the repair on Windows/Linux Node24, while patched full runtime suites pass158 plus lint/types per platform. Manual owner finding, not a prospective paid-Scout trial.

Shared attachment helper rechecks isDone after registration and removes only its own just-added listener. Native tests retain unrelated data/error listeners and verify exact cancellation reasons. Fork patch only, not an upstream PR or merge.
